title: Augmented rational complex of a proper product interval
statement: Let $r\geq0$ and $m\in\mathbf N^r$. Give $\mathbf N^r$ its coordinatewise order and put $T_m=\{v\in\mathbf N^r:v\leq m,\ v\ne0,\ v\ne m\}$. For $n\geq0$ let $B_{m,n}$ be the set of strict chains with $n$ vertices in $T_m$, equivalently order embeddings $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\hookrightarrow T_m$, and let $C_{m,n}=\mathbf Q^{(B_{m,n})}$. In particular $B_{m,0}$ consists of the empty chain. Define $d_n:C_{m,n+1}\to C_{m,n}$ by $d_n[v_0<\cdots<v_n]=\sum_{a=0}^n(-1)^a[v_0<\cdots<\widehat v_a<\cdots<v_n]$. Thus $d_0$ sends each vertex to the empty-chain generator. Double-deletion cancellation gives $d_n d_{n+1}=0$. Define the augmented chain complex $A(m)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] by placing $C_{m,n}$ in integer degree $n-1$, with these differentials, and extending by zero below degree $-1$. Its degree $-1$ term is canonically $\mathbf Q$ on the empty chain and its degree $k\geq0$ term is free on strict chains with $k+1$ vertices.
